body:
Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (1) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. A damaged block restores an old lead ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: a781937

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The regex-based STATE_BLOCK/BROKEN_BLOCK parsing is replaced by a strict line-based parser:
>fenced_blocks/locate_block require the agent-room-state block to be the first fenced block, unique,
>with a closing fence, and with only key: value body lines (each key once); otherwise BlockUnreadable
>is raised. A quoted same-info copy now causes an invalid block (two blocks), so pushed_lease walks
>back to the last valid commit instead of trusting the damaged tip. commit path refuses duplicate
>blocks via check_missions/locate_block. Damaged fences are renamed to agent-room-state-damaged
>rather than spanning content, so a later fence can no longer be consumed as the closer. This
>addresses the finding with a different implementation than the suggested regex-based fix.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>STATE_BLOCK can treat a later fence as the missing closing fence, and read_block accepts the
>first parseable matching block even if it is a quoted copy below the real one. After an outside edit
>damages either fence, an old lease copied into mission notes can become authoritative without a
>warning, allowing a superseded lead to post, close the room, or reuse a counter.
>
>
2. Recovery can move the project checkout ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: a781937

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The commit removes the cwd-based is_stale_state_worktree/project_toplevel logic and replaces it with
>a candidate-directory check. has_marker() inspects the candidate's own git dir for the STATE_MARKER
>file that room.py writes only into worktrees/clones it creates, so the project checkout (no marker,
>no state history) is refused regardless of cwd. state_checkout() now resolves the project root from
>--git-common-dir rather than cwd-relative toplevel, and ensure_worktree() computes root before
>moving anything. check_state_dir refuses directories without the marker, and
>t_only_marked_dirs_are_moved tests the project checkout being refused from work, tmp and a builder
>worktree. The approach differs from the suggested Git-metadata inspection but addresses the same
>hazard.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>is_stale_state_worktree identifies the project checkout through the process's current directory
>rather than the directory it is about to move. If ROOM_STATE_DIR names a detached project checkout
>and the command runs from elsewhere, ensure_worktree can rename that checkout and replace its path
>with a state worktree, disrupting linked builder worktrees.
>
>
3. Block repair erases mission records ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: a781937

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The fix removes the BROKEN_BLOCK span-based replacement in with_block. The new code never deletes
>text through a damaged fence: write_block/locate_block parse the block strictly (only the first
>fenced block with info string agent-room-state counts, closed by a bare fence), and when the block
>is invalid with_block renames every agent-room-state fence to agent-room-state-damaged in place and
>prepends a fresh canonical block under the title. Nothing between fences is removed, matching the
>suggested approach of prepending a valid block and retiring the damaged fence while preserving
>prose. Also the regex-based BROKEN_BLOCK/STATE_BLOCK constants are replaced by the fence-line
>parser.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>BROKEN_BLOCK can span from a damaged opening fence to a later fence in the mission notes, and
>with_block replaces that entire span with a restored block. If an outside edit also removes the
>block's closing fence, the next state write can delete intervening mission tables, tasks, and parked
>questions from the pushed file.
>
>

4. Preflight can report no admin bypass when it couldn't read the ruleset ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: a781937

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>Added an unread list in cmd_preflight that records each ruleset id whose detail request returned
>non-200 or a non-dict response. After the bypass loop, it appends "couldn't read ruleset <id>, so
>its bypass actors are unknown" to the bypass list, which makes the check print a "!" warning instead
>of "✓ admin bypass: none". This follows the suggested fix's approach (track unreadable rulesets,
>report unknown) though the warning text differs slightly from the suggested format. A regression
>test t_preflight_approving_reviews was also added.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>cmd_preflight stores {} for a failed or non-dict ruleset-detail response without recording that
>the ruleset could not be inspected. When branch rules identify that ruleset, the bypass check finds
>no actors in the empty dictionary and can print ✓ admin bypass: none instead of an unknown
>warning, because its existing error path covers only protection and branch-rules requests.
>
>
5. One lead can hide messages from another ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: a781937

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>Cursor files are now keyed per room, role and session (cursor_file uses session_id()), so two lead
>sessions on one machine no longer move each other's read cursor; a new test t_two_leads_one_machine
>asserts separate cursor files and independent reads.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>unseen now distinguishes leads by session, but cursor_file still stores one cursor per room and
>role. When two lead sessions share a machine, the first lead's read advances the second lead's
>cursor past architect messages that the second has not seen.
>
>
6. Recovery strands unpushed state commits ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: a781937

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The fix adds save_local_work(), which, before a stale state worktree is moved aside, commits its
>HEAD and uncommitted changes to a durable ref (refs/agent-room/broken-<stamp>) in the project
>repository, falling back to a patch file if that fails. move_aside() now takes save=True from
>ensure_worktree() and reports the saved ref in its notice. This preserves the unpushed commit under
>a durable ref rather than checking and refusing, a different but valid implementation of the
>suggested "preserve HEAD under a durable ref" remediation. Tests
>t_stale_worktree_local_work_is_saved verify the unpushed commit is kept.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>ensure_worktree moves a stale linked state worktree aside without checking whether it contains
>local changes or unpushed commits. When it prunes and recreates the worktree at the original path,
>the moved copy's Git administrative link can point at the replacement, leaving its earlier commit
>without a normal ref or reflog.
>
>
View medium (2)
7. A lead inside stale state cannot recover ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: a781937

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The commit makes ensure_worktree resolve the project checkout before anything moves ("root =
>state_checkout()  # before anything moves: the current directory may be inside the one moved
>aside"), and uses that stable root for ls_heads(root) and for the later worktree/clone recreation.
>state_checkout() now returns the main worktree via --git-common-dir, never a state clone, so
>recovery Git operations run from a stable location. The stale-worktree check is also reworked to
>recognize candidates by a STATE_MARKER written by room.py (mark(path)), independent of the invoking
>cwd, and save_local_work runs before the move. Together this addresses running recovery from inside
>the directory being replaced, which is the finding's premise and requested remediation.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>ensure_worktree rebuilds a stale state directory while Git commands and checkout discovery still
>depend on the invoking directory. When a lead runs a state command from inside a state worktree
>whose branch was recreated, clone-mode recovery can refuse it and linked-worktree recovery can fail
>partway through after moving it.
>
>
8. Weakened tests evade the merge hold 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>The M3 gate specification says a merge-hold bullet containing deleted matches only deleted paths,
>while the default playbook puts deleted and weakened tests in that same bullet. An edit to an
>existing test therefore matches the test globs but does not trigger the sensitive-path hold required
>by the governing design.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[docs/design/m3-reviews-gate.md[109]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/6/files#diff-1d80bc747f61196b20f463418d4f5a8ed63e17504c309ba79834aa3278ce332fR109-R109) > >```diff >+6. **Sensitive paths:** the changed paths (`git diff --name-status origin/main...HEAD`) against the globs of the "## Merge-hold list" section of `PLAYBOOK.md` on the state branch. The template has one bullet per area, ``-
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The new specification excludes non-deletions for the template's combined test bullet, whereas v1
>includes weakened tests among sensitive changes and requires matching paths to fail the gate.
>
> > [docs/design/m3-reviews-gate.md\[108-109\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/a7819374fe298f7392e483186191e470f51bce15/docs/design/m3-reviews-gate.md/#L108-L109) > [templates/playbook/PLAYBOOK.md\[23-31\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/a7819374fe298f7392e483186191e470f51bce15/templates/playbook/PLAYBOOK.md/#L23-L31) > [docs/design/v1.md\[215-229\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/a7819374fe298f7392e483186191e470f51bce15/docs/design/v1.md/#L215-L229) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The deleted-only rule exempts modified tests from the default sensitive-path hold, including modifications that weaken them. >## Fix Focus Areas >- docs/design/m3-reviews-gate.md[108-109] >- templates/playbook/PLAYBOOK.md[27-31] >## Recommended Fix >Specify a conservative hold for modified tests unless a reliable weakened-test determination is available. Keep the template labels and gate matching rules aligned with that behavior. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/db26aaf6-31bd-4f77-bfc8-88567e336b51?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/db26aaf6-31bd-4f77-bfc8-88567e336b51)

9. A failed git diff makes state commit report 'nothing to commit' ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: a781937

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The diff stores the result of git diff --cached --quiet in staged, raises StateError with git's
>stderr when returncode is neither 0 nor 1, and commits only when returncode == 1. This is exactly
>the suggested fix. A regression test t_failed_git_diff_is_an_error was also added.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>commit_and_push runs git diff --cached --quiet with check=False and commits only when it
>returns exactly 1. Any other failure, such as exit 128 from a broken index, is treated as 'no staged
>changes'. With no unpushed commits, state commit then prints nothing to commit and exits 0,
>while the edits stay unpushed in the worktree.
>
>
10. Preflight --fix failure prints no reason ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: a781937

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The --fix handler now computes why = str(e) or 'the state branch moved; run it again' and prints it,
>so an empty StateMoved produces the retry hint instead of an empty reason.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>The --fix handler formats {e or 'the state branch moved; run it again'}, but an exception object
>is always truthy, so a bare StateMoved() (empty message) wins over the fallback. When the
>lead-files push loses a race during preflight --fix, the output reads `lead-owned files: --fix
>failed: ` with no explanation and no hint to retry.
>
>

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
